🎯 A moment from this week:

Job boards have been slower than usual on a few of my current searches.

So instead of waiting on postings, I've been leaning more on community colleges, university career centers and professional associations. It takes more effort up front than posting a role and hoping. But it gives me people to talk to when the applications aren't coming in.

The takeaway: some of the strongest pipelines aren't job boards at all. Relationships with career centers and associations tied to your field can be more reliable than waiting for the right application to come in.

text:
Networking advice that says 'just be genuine' is not actually advice.

Telling anxious job seekers to just network authentically is like telling someone with stage fright to just relax. Real networking guidance is specific: here's exactly what to say, here's how to follow up, here's what to do when someone doesn't respond. Vague encouragement isn't a strategy.

What's one specific networking script or approach that's actually worked for you?

text:
🎯 A moment from this week:

I've seen the same pattern more than once. A candidate we were excited about simply stops responding.

Not a no. Not a request to reschedule. Just silence.

Sometimes the reason behind it is completely reasonable. But from the hiring side, all we see is that the candidate went quiet.

The takeaway: a two-line email saying you need to reschedule keeps the door open. Going quiet closes it, even when the reason you disappeared was completely reasonable.

Job seekers: if something comes up before an interview, send the two lines. It takes a minute and it can save the opportunity.

#JobSearchTips #InterviewTips #NeoHRUS

text:
How do the right people find me, trust me, and open the door?

Once you know where you're going, you build the road there. Path runs three tracks in parallel: a brand that shows your impact at a glance, a network inside your target companies, and focused applications that actually get through. Strategy beats volume at every step.

Your goal for this phase: A resume and LinkedIn that tell one quantified story, a weekly outreach rhythm, and a steady flow of tailored, logged applications you can justify.

What's the story you want a recruiter to walk away with after six seconds on your profile?

Watch out for: Underselling your achievements ("helped with," "assisted with") and spray-and-pray applying to feel busy. Silence from outreach isn't rejection, response rates are naturally low.

You're ready to move on when: Your resume and LinkedIn match with numbers attached, you've logged five informational interviews, and you have a weekly rhythm of tailored applications.

In the Spine of Your Job Search playbook: Modules 2-4: Brand Yourself, Network with a Purpose, Apply Smarter
